originality.rationale: The accepted scientific contribution is the precise coexistence of period-total negative-real-axis stability with a sharp, explicitly evaluated fixed-b singular stationary noise gain for standard alternating AB2. Inspected primary sources do not establish this joint statement. Earlier Nordsieck stability articles are relevant historical prior art and their unavailable full text is recorded as a residual precedence risk; generic stationary Lyapunov theory supplies technique but not the evaluated sharp coefficient.
residual_risks: The 1983 and 1989 Nordsieck stability primary full texts were unavailable; an earlier equivalent deterministic period-two stability classification is possible.
A specialist periodic-AR or numerical-roundoff study might already evaluate the exact stationary coefficient under a mathematically equivalent normalization, despite the negative searches.
The iid additive perturbation model is an analytic benchmark and is not automatically the error law of floating-point arithmetic.

value.rationale: Step-ratio degeneration in a standard variable-step Adams method creates a sharp quadratic stationary noise amplification despite an unchanged period-total stability threshold and a limiting spectral radius bounded below one. The explicit positive all-b coefficient is a structural diagnostic for the distinction between Floquet stability and perturbation robustness. It is not a mere parameter substitution into the constant-step AB2 table or an arbitrary isolated computation.
